sequences.title: Wavefunctions · returning, relating, composing
sequences.thread: A body can return without occupying the same state. A trace makes that return inspectable; projection and phase let repetition organise space; excitation and composition make several returns act together.
sequences.necessity: A specified state or coordinate, a reference for progression, and a rule relating them. Distinguish a dynamically integrated pendulum from a prescribed sine, and a moving pattern from transport of matter.
sequences.handoff: Formfinding precedes Waves on the current spine. Carry equilibrium and restoring behaviour into oscillation. Leave Waves able to distinguish a complex appearance from an unspecified process; Randomness then asks what a procedure chooses.
sequences.route: Keep the current six-room museum route for the first implementation. Unit Circle and Propagation are strong candidates for later insertion between the trace and Sine Space, after their footprints are repaired. Bernini, Cage, Sky Stairs and TrigWalkingPath remain independently developed extension rooms. Recheck transitions against the route actually shipped.

sequences.title: Randomness · choosing, accumulating, excluding
sequences.thread: A reproducible procedure supplies choices; an eligibility rule and distribution decide their possibilities; accumulated choices form paths and populations; feedback and uncertain timing alter what a body can do.
sequences.necessity: A defined outcome space and selection procedure. Seed/state, draw order, distribution, boundary and interpretation are different decisions. A histogram cannot recover the order it discarded.
sequences.handoff: The five-harmonic sum is repeatable without looking simple. Start here by replaying an irregular-looking field. Finish with a body planning around random waits; Noise asks how neighbouring samples can be related.
sequences.route: Keep the seven active halls while improving all fourteen authored maps. The extension rooms supply concrete routes into estimation, feedback and correlation; they are not automatically extra museum halls. In particular Random_Space_Geometry and Random_Space overlap the next sequence: use them as comparison laboratories, not duplicate introductory lectures.

sequences.title: Noise · neighbouring, sampling, inhabiting
sequences.thread: A spatial relation constrains variation. A field becomes colour, relief, occupied volume or a route through distinct reading rules. Layers and coordinate warps expand what those fields can do; fair comparisons reveal which change actually mattered.
sequences.necessity: A sampling domain and coordinates, a field-generating rule, and a mapping from values into an appearance or consequence. Correlation alone supplies no stored history, collision, ecology or intention.
sequences.handoff: Contrast a new random draw with revisiting a coordinate in a fixed field. The current next chapter is Cellular Automata: a field supplies related values; an automaton maintains state and updates it through a neighbourhood rule. Do not promise a return to Lab_Path on the main route unless navigation is deliberately changed.
sequences.route: Keep six active halls. Repair the Perlin/Simplex claim first. Develop domain warping and walkable noise as extension rooms; decide later whether they earn main-route slots. Lab_Path is a short optional reflective exit, not another long noise lesson.

maps.body: A suspended body; the player's releasing hand.

Preserve this contract; see recovery.html and the dated doc/space archive.

Start with one release experiment. Offer a deliberate reveal of angle and signed angular velocity, using the existing evidence modes where suitable. If a damping comparison is added, change only that setting; do not introduce every regime at once.

Check the initial cube collection against old map structure before consolidating. Preserve meaningful stationary/prescribed-motion examples so a calculated pendulum is distinguishable from a cube following sin(time).
book: Open with two visits to the centre that travel in opposite directions; invite a release before explaining.
Describe position, direction and turning points, then connect the short integration excerpt to the force work already learned.
Let a second release trouble a prediction. Avoid promising exact small-angle behaviour at large releases.
End with the need to keep a record: the next room gives elapsed history a spatial direction.
